candidates.title: Compare learned agent pruning with matched random pruning
candidates.rule: When evaluating multi-agent pruning, include a single-agent baseline and random pruning at the same structural budget, and measure aggregation overhead rather than counting removed edges alone.
candidates.passage: an edge-pruning method can look cheaper under an edge-count or edge-passing metric while becoming more expensive
candidates.finding: Across twenty main-grid cells, learned pruning averages -0.77 accuracy points relative to the original system versus -0.44 for matched random pruning. Some methods add a decision node that increases prompt traffic despite fewer edges. The evaluation recommendation is inferred from these comparisons.
models: Small open-weight 4B–8B backbones pinned by task family
candidates.conditions: Shared model, agent registry, prompts and runtime isolate structural changes; assess whether the unpruned team improves over a single agent in the first place.
candidates.limitations: Whitespace token counts are proxies, not provider billing. Shared prompts exclude method-specific prompt engineering. Uncertainty analysis covers only one family and conclusions do not cover all team-construction methods.
candidates.validation_test: At matched model and runtime compare unpruned, learned-pruned, several random-pruned and single-agent systems. Include final aggregator, tools, optimization spend and quality uncertainty.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
